newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Guilder rates hold steady, but may wobble next week.
newsitem.headline: Guilder rates hold steady, but may wobble next week.

text.p: Dutch money market rates held largely steady in routine Thursday trade, although overnight guilders eased fractionally in the run-up to next Friday's expiry of the secured loans pact.
Dealers said the unusually short secured loans pact, coupled with the imminent long weekend was making it difficult for market players to gauge their liquidity needs with a great degree of precision.
"Most operators are playing it safe, making sure they have enough liquidity to tide them over the Whitsun weekend," one dealer said.
As a result there was a possibility that call money rates could drop sharply on Tuesday as market players started to use up their savings under the secured loans pact, some dealers speculated.
But call rates next week will also be heavily influenced by tomorrow's allocation under the new special advances pact and the spread of liquidity between the various players.
The Dutch central bank earlier announced a new seven-day short-term liquidity pact at an unchanged rate of 2.9 percent.
Overnight guilders are currently quoting at 3.12-3.25 percent bid/offer, but could come down to as little as 2.5 percent next week if Friday's allocation is ample.
The guilder was pegged at 112.445 per 100 marks at Thursday's fixing, firming slightly from Wednesday's 112.45.
